judgements.justification: A's highest score, KMnW's 8, praised the formulation in one sentence, then listed faults, and only said 'I keep my recommendation'; no reviewer argued for the paper on a detailed reading.
No reviewer admitted reading only part of the paper; YnSg's high-confidence 7 admitted it could not judge significance, but it supported A and its objections did not set the tone.
Both committees judged SNIPS within the score-based posterior-sampling framing; no reviewer contested the premise from another theoretical tradition.

A's meta-review argued only that 'the majority opinion is that the results are strong enough to warrant publication', conceded the innovation over [19] is weak, and gave no case for the spotlight tier.
Reviewers in both committees saw that the paper had no baseline and asked for comparisons (A: nVFq, y4bh, YnSg; B: GwuL); neither committee took reported comparisons at face value.
A's meta-review omitted the missing baselines, but in the direction of the higher decision; B's meta-review misread the method, not the reviewers' final positions, which were all below threshold.
Questions about realistic applications (nVFq, kSnH) concerned the prior's image classes, not a narrow audience or a better-suited venue, and neither committee set its tier on breadth.
A's lone detractor nVFq was principled (no baselines, no ablation, novelty over [19]), and A's AC did not argue against that score instead of weighing a higher tier.
Neither forum received new experiments; the PnP/RED comparisons were only promised, on both forums.
B's confidences were 3, 4, 4, 4 with no high-confidence expert rating above the others, and A's high-confidence 8 aligned with the majority that set the tier.
B's three late score drops cited baselines and Section 3 clarity, objections raised in the original reviews and answered by the authors; GwuL's unanswered follow-up changed no score.
At posting the committees rated similarly (8, 7, 7 plus a reject against 7, 7, 6, 4); the final gap came from score moves in discussion, not from scoring leniency.
Neither committee judged the headline claim or title overstated; the narrowed wordings concerned the description of prior literature.
A's supporters committed to 7, 7 and 8, and B's reviewers fell below threshold; no committee converged on marginal-accept scores.
